headline: Cabinet reshuffle: 4 new ministers and 2 state ministers assigned portfolios
summary: The Cabinet Division has published a gazette distributing roles among the newly sworn-in ministers, including new appointments for LGRD, Information, and Civil Aviation.
details: The Cabinet Division on Friday published a gazette distributing portfolios among four ministers and two state ministers after they took oath at Bangabhaban.

Abdul Moyeen Khan has been appointed as the minister for local government, rural development and co-operatives (LGRD), while Saching Prue has been appointed minister for Chittagong Hill Tracts affairs.
Andaleeve Rahman Partho has been appointed as the information and broadcasting minister, replacing Zahir Uddin Swapan.
Rashiduzzaman Millat has been assigned the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism as a full minister.
Incumbent minister Afroza Khanam Rita has been reassigned as the food minister.
Humaiun Kobir has been appointed state minister for foreign affairs, and Md Shamim Kaiser has been given responsibility as state minister for religious affairs.
caption:
New faces in the cabinet! 🇧🇩

Four ministers and two state ministers have officially received their portfolios.

The Cabinet Division on Friday published a gazette distributing portfolios among four ministers and two state ministers after they took oath at Bangabhaban.

Abdul Moyeen Khan has been appointed as the minister for local government, rural development and co-operatives (LGRD), while Saching Prue has been appointed minister for Chittagong Hill Tracts affairs.

Andaleeve Rahman Partho has been appointed as the information and broadcasting minister, replacing Zahir Uddin Swapan.

Rashiduzzaman Millat has been assigned the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism as a full minister.

Incumbent minister Afroza Khanam Rita has been reassigned as the food minister.

Humaiun Kobir has been appointed state minister for foreign affairs, and Md Shamim Kaiser has been given responsibility as state minister for religious affairs.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: Mirza Fakhrul [[takes oath as 23rd President]] of Bangladesh
headline: Mirza Fakhrul takes oath as 23rd President of Bangladesh
summary: The veteran BNP leader won the first contested presidential race since 1991, defeating Col (retd) Oli Ahmed with 255 votes.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has officially taken oath as the 23rd President of Bangladesh at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban on Friday evening.
The oath was administered by Speaker-in-charge Barrister Kayser Kamal, with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and other high-ranking officials in attendance.
Fakhrul was elected on Thursday with 255 votes, defeating the Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance candidate Col (retd) Oli Ahmed, who received 88 votes.
This election marked the country's first contested presidential race since 1991.
A veteran BNP leader and former secretary general of the party, Fakhrul resigned from his party post on August 13 after being nominated for the presidency.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expressed his best wishes for a successful and dignified tenure, emphasizing a commitment to democracy and constitutional dignity.
Presidents of India, Pakistan, and Nepal have already sent congratulations to the new head of state.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd President of Bangladesh. He won the first contested presidential race since the 1991.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has officially taken oath as the 23rd President of Bangladesh at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban on Friday evening.

The oath was administered by Speaker-in-charge Barrister Kayser Kamal, with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and other high-ranking officials in attendance.

Fakhrul was elected on Thursday with 255 votes, defeating the Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance candidate Col (retd) Oli Ahmed, who received 88 votes.

This election marked the country's first contested presidential race since 1991.

A veteran BNP leader and former secretary general of the party, Fakhrul resigned from his party post on August 13 after being nominated for the presidency.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expressed his best wishes for a successful and dignified tenure, emphasizing a commitment to democracy and constitutional dignity.

Presidents of India, Pakistan, and Nepal have already sent congratulations to the new head of state.
